title: Dense full fine-tune and dense LoRA at 4k-16k
what: Reference loss-vs-FLOPs curves (probes every 10 steps to step 100). Every speedup on this page is read against these.
result: Held-out CE at step 50 / 100: dense full FT 0.176 / 0.135, dense LoRA LR 1e-5 0.170 / 0.131, dense LoRA LR 2e-5 0.126 at step 100 (dense LoRA costs 0.74x dense per step). The reference is the cheaper of the three at each loss level.

title: Current recipe (router, keep 20% after block 7, 7% after block 16)
what: The 8k recipe unchanged at 4k-16k on the new tasks, plus random keep at the same budget.
result: Recipe: 0.22x dense per step, 1.7x fewer FLOPs than the tuned dense-LoRA reference to the 100-step level, 1.4x on the worst task. Random keep at the same budget: 0.54x of the recipe's efficiency; random keep 9%: 0.42x; keep 10%/3.5%: 0.71x; 5%/2%: 0.55x; 2%/1%: 0.27x.

title: Frozen no-grad prefix + earlier cuts
what: Blocks 0-k run forward-only (no backward, no stored activations), tokens dropped from block 2-4 onward in more stages. Attacks the 0.2x/step floor of blocks 0-6 and the memory peak.
result: Negative. Freezing blocks 0-6 (forward-only) with the recipe's cuts: 0.149x dense per step, 0.282 held-out CE at step 60 vs about 0.19 for the recipe; deeper freezing is worse (0.399 / 0.491 / 0.647 with the boundary at block 7 / 16 / 20 plus earlier cuts). Earlier cuts alone (first cut at block 2) also trail the recipe per FLOP. Transient memory is unchanged under activation checkpointing. The gradient into the early blocks carries most of the learning. Branch loop/prefix.

title: Gold-aware stochastic keep
what: Per-document keep probability raised for gold documents but never 1 and never 0 for distractors, so the kept set does not reveal the answer; drop before block 0 as well as mid-stack.
result: Mixed. Best arm grJ (0.133x dense per step): 1.26x the recipe at matched loss on the main pool at step 108, but on the 50/50 pool gold-aware arms are level with or behind the plain recipe on that pool, so the two gains do not stack. The cheapest arms (0.07-0.08x) stay shallow (0.27-0.34 held-out CE).

title: Loss and backward through the first few blocks only
what: An early-exit answer loss after block k gives true per-token gradients at full length for the cost of k blocks; use them to pick tokens and to train the early blocks.
result: Negative. Selecting tokens by the gradient of an early-exit answer loss is worse than the ridge router at the recipe's keep (0.213 vs 0.175 held-out CE at step 75) and at 10%/3% (0.237 vs 0.224); it only wins at a very aggressive cut after block 2 (0.584 vs 0.763 at step 40), far from any reference level. The auxiliary early loss slows training; training the early blocks by the early loss alone fails (0.503). The frozen head at block 7 gives an early-exit CE near uniform, so its gradient is weak. Branch loop/earlyloss.

title: Detached context / reused context states
what: Context tokens run forward-only (or reuse cached states), gradient only through query and answer tokens; then drop context tokens aggressively in that no-grad pass.
result: Negative for FLOPs. Context forward-only from block 0, no drops: 0.15x of the recipe's efficiency; from block 7: 0.354 at step 97; from block 16: 0.207 at 131 PF vs the recipe's 0.145; with a 1,024-token gradient tail: 0.375 at step 173; every 4th step dense: 0.44x of the recipe. The memory arms with activation checkpointing off produced no result. Branch loop/detach.

title: FLOP-aware row sampling and row skipping
what: Sample rows by expected loss decrease per FLOP (short rows more often, a tail of 16k rows), skip rows a cheap early-exit loss marks as solved.
result: Recipe on rows <= 5k: 3.2-3.4x vs dense LoRA down to held-out CE 0.125, then it plateaus at 0.119 (no 8k / 16k rows). Length curriculum on the 50/50 pool: 2.7-3.4x, no better than the static mix. Token-budget batches help dense LoRA (1.4-1.5x) more than the recipe.

title: Label-consistent sub-problems
what: Train on a random subset of a row's documents with the answer rewritten for the subset (reorder, qdmatch), mixed with a few full rows.
result: Works. Recipe on the 80/20 short/long pool: 3.1-3.4x fewer FLOPs than dense LoRA at held-out CE 0.125 (two seeds); 50/50 pool: 2.9-3.0x; plain recipe 1.9-2.2x. Short rows alone fall behind. Dense LoRA on the same pools gains less (1.4-1.5x with token-budget batches). Next: 90% and 95% short, long tail only at 16k, short part only at 1k, full-epoch runs. On the 16k rows alone the mixed pools are only about 1.1-1.2x ahead of the plain recipe (56 rows, noisy).

title: Skip the FFN for context tokens
what: Context tokens stay in attention / GDN mixing but skip most FFNs, instead of leaving the sequence.
result: Negative. Body tokens skipping the FFN in blocks 0-6 with probability 0.5: 0.193x dense per step (the recipe is 0.220x) but 0.274 held-out CE at step 50 vs the recipe's 0.201. Skipping every body-token FFN in blocks 0-3 stops learning (0.779 at step 50): training adapts to FFN-free tokens and the dense eval forward runs every FFN. Ceiling of the idea: the FFN is 41-62% of a block's per-token FLOPs. Branch loop/ffnskip.

title: Start from a base with token-drop continued pre-training
what: Look for existing drop-CPT checkpoints and test whether aggressive dropping loses less from such a base. No CPT runs inside the loop.
result: Router recipe from the token-exit CPT base and the dense-CPT control: 0.65-0.77x of the recipe's efficiency at matched loss, no better than the standard base at the same keep (0.71x at keep 10%/3.5%). No benefit from the drop-CPT base in this proxy.

title: LR, batch size and schedule per FLOP
what: Cheap arms can afford more, smaller steps: rows per step, LR and warmup tuned per FLOP rather than per step.
result: Recipe at LR 2e-5: 0.85x; LR 4e-5: 0.61x; 8 rows/step: 0.74x; 8 rows/step at LR 2e-5: 0.62x of the recipe's efficiency at matched loss. Dense LoRA: LR 2e-5 slightly better than 1e-5 (0.126 vs 0.131 at step 100), LR 4e-5 worse (0.170).

title: Drop-CPT bases fine-tuned in their own token-exit format
what: Token exit at block 8 and at the input (first+last rule), from the matching CPT base and from the standard base, at fixed compression 0.2 / 0.1 / 0.05.
result: Negative. Input-level token exit (first+last rule, keep 5-10%) improves for 25-50 steps and then degrades on the dense probe from both the standard and the drop-CPT base (never below 0.69). Exit at block 8, keep 10%: 0.233 (CPT base) vs 0.238 (standard base) at step 93, a tie, both behind the recipe. The CPT bases start 0.25-0.32 held-out CE worse than the standard base on these tasks.

title: Multi-question rows
what: Each row keeps its original question and answer, then appends 8-32 short sub-questions derived from its gold (which passage follows X, which document matches query j, which claim contradicts claim i, is document i an outlier). The context is paid for once; the extra answers cost only their own tokens.
result: Negative. Recipe on multi-question rows: 0.124 held-out CE at 220 PF vs the plain recipe's 0.124 at 180-210 PF; on the 50/50 pool 0.124 at 161 PF vs 0.125 at 135 PF. The sub-answers add 2-3x the supervised tokens but dilute the main answer's loss; a weighted variant was not tried.

title: Loss-proportional task and length sampling
what: Sample the next rows by each task-and-length cell's running training loss per FLOP instead of uniformly (reorder holds 5x the loss of the other tasks); row-level backward skipping; per-row vs per-token loss averaging.
result: No gain at 16k. Loss-per-cost sampling of task and length cells is level with the plain recipe on the same pool on the 16k held-out rows (1.0x on the 80/20 pool with two seeds, 0.9-1.0x on the 50/50 pool); its all-lengths gain is 1.0-1.3x and does not stack on the 80/20 pool. A stronger cost term (0.22 PF per step) stops the 16k loss tracking (0.90x). A 16k-targeted rule is level with the recipe at matched FLOPs. Loss-only sampling and a static reorder-heavy mix are level; per-row loss averaging starves reorder. No task is starved by the loss-per-cost rules. Branch loop/alloc.

title: Length-scaling breakdown and document-local attention in the early blocks
what: Tabulate where the recipe's FLOPs go at 4k-128k rows (the full-length attention of the early blocks is quadratic in length), then make that attention document-local during training so the early blocks' cost grows linearly with length.
result: FLOP breakdown done (flop meter's own formulas; the model has 32 blocks, 8 full attention at blocks 3, 7, ..., 31 and 24 Gated DeltaNet). Recipe cost vs dense: 0.227 / 0.217 / 0.189 / 0.168 at 4k / 16k / 64k / 128k. The only early full-attention block is block 3: its full-length attention is 4% of the recipe's step at 16k, 15% at 64k, 25% at 128k; making it document-local would give 1.04x / 1.17x / 1.33x at 16k / 64k / 128k. The floor is the length-independent per-token cost of blocks 0-6 (FFN, GDN, projections): 0.118x dense, 54% of the recipe's step at 16k. Proxy runs with document-local attention (block 3; blocks 3-15; all attention blocks) are running. Proxy at 16k (one seed): local attention in block 3 only trains normally and is 0.01-0.02 held-out CE behind the recipe per step (0.246 / 0.181 / 0.163 / 0.143 vs 0.229 / 0.172 / 0.140 / 0.124) for a 2% FLOP saving; local attention also in blocks 7, 11, 15 stalls training (0.773 / 0.762 / 0.570 / 0.390). A causal-mask control of the same attention path is running to rule out a bug in the later blocks.

title: Memory that stays flat at 256k-1M tokens
what: Measure how peak training memory grows with row length (16k-256k) for dense LoRA and the recipe, then run the early blocks chunk by chunk (no-grad pass, later blocks on the kept tokens, second chunked pass with gradient) with a kept-token budget fixed in tokens, so the peak is one chunk plus the kept tokens instead of the whole row.
result: Scaling law measured (transient above a 24.5 GiB baseline, one H200, micro-batch 1): dense LoRA 0.37 GiB per 1k tokens (52 GiB at 128k, out of memory at 256k); recipe 0.24 GiB per 1k (34 GiB at 128k). Chunked early blocks with 8k chunks: forward exact, gradient cosine 0.996 overall and 0.982 in blocks 0-6. Proxy runs and the memory sweep of the chunked method are next.
